title: [CQ-F03] Structured execution contract
description:
Objective: Extend existing task and submit_plan contract with intended behavior, criteria, invariants, compatibility, approved scope, reuse/source assumptions and check references.

Deliverable: Structured execution contract. This is task F03 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): F02, M01.
definitionOfDone: Material changes advance planRevision through the same durable task write.
Sanitization, bounds and producer/consumer schema tests prevent silent contract loss.
Fresh verification `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

(1) Add `export interface TaskExecutionContract` (just above `interface Task`) with exactly these eight optional keys, in this order: `intendedBehavior?: string` (observable behavior/outcome the change must produce); `acceptanceCriteria?: string[]` (behavior-level criteria; definitionOfDone stays the human-owned list); `invariants?: string[]`; `compatibility?: string[]` (legacy data, wire/protocol shapes and callers that must keep working); `approvedScope?: string[]` (symbols, interfaces and producer->consumer surfaces the change may touch - FILE scope stays each step's affectedFiles/newFiles, there is no second file list); `reuse?: string[]` (existing implementations reused, or why a new one is introduced); `sourceAssumptions?: string[]` (source facts the plan relies on, with path/symbol references); `checkRefs?: string[]` (required verification, each exactly as it will be run). Execution status, startedAt/completedAt, reported modifiedFiles, progress notes, amendment audit fields and inactive amendment history are NOT material; reopen neither resets it nor advances it by clearing execution evidence. Keep the existing domain, caller-stamp stripping and legacy-absent-is-0 sentences.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Decisions taken with defaults (TURBO; recorded here and in a task comment):
1. One optional Task.executionContract object with eight flat fields (intendedBehavior string + seven string lists). Rejected: a separate contract store or contract revision counter (epic rail: one approval revision authority, no parallel stores); nesting into ImplementationStep or DoD strings (loses structure; DoD stays human-owned).
2. No file list inside the contract: file scope stays the steps' affectedFiles/newFiles, which F02 already treats as approved scope. approvedScope names symbols/interfaces/producer->consumer surfaces. Avoids two disagreeing sources of file scope.
3. Strict validation at every writer (submit_plan and taskStore.updateTask), sharing one set of bounds; never a slicing sanitizer. Slicing is the 5000/10000 step-description truncation bug class that DoD item 3 forbids.
4. Contract text gets a forbidden-pattern scan only. Folding it into the required-pattern check would weaken the steps' required-pattern rail; skipping the scan would let a forbidden token ride in approval text (same reasoning that put newFiles into the rail text).
5. Replace semantics on resubmission: a contract describes the plan it was submitted with, so an omitted contract clears a stored one (key sent only when there is something to set or clear, keeping legacy payloads byte-identical).
6. get_context projects the stored value raw, consistent with implementationPlan; stored contracts are canonical by construction. A compact packet/role-trim redesign is CQ-C01's job.
7. Kept as ONE task despite 8 distinct files (warn >5, hard cap 10): producer, store, consumer and docs must change together for the contract to be persisted AND served, and the docs fix was explicitly requested by F02 QA. Splitting would add a dependency hop in front of F04-F12.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: taskStore.updateTask is the single chokepoint for every task writer (submit_plan, amend_plan_step, reopen, request_replan, plugin UPDATE_TASK); order is sanitize -> guards -> derivePlanRevision -> writeEntity -> map.set -> activity -> emit. derivePlanRevision bumps once per write via sameSanitizedSurface (structural; array order significant, key order not). validators.ts has two families: validate* throws before disk, sanitize* never throws; reuse requirePlainObject, rejectUnknownFields and validateStringValue (truncate:false, allowNewlines:true). validateStringArrayValue truncates and forbids newlines, so do not reuse it. get_context's task payload is projected field by field (a new Task field is invisible until projected); ROLE_OMITTED/trimForQa trim QA/worker views. submit_plan's rails check (util/rails.ts checkPlanRails) is a lowercase substring scan of step text plus files. ToolTestHarness writes raw task JSON (good for seeding legacy/corrupt rows); its project forbids 'rm -rf'. F01 held-out approvalRevision.acceptance.test.ts has no F03 group and must stay unchanged. EOL: schema.ts, taskStore.ts and validators.ts are CRLF; submitPlan.ts, getContext.ts and docs are LF. isEpicFinal shows true only because this row's order (225.5) is the epic's highest; F12 remains the real integration/hardening task, so do not widen scope to whole-epic integration.
